findings.title: Async legacy writes run on the request context, which is cancelled once the request returns
findings.body: Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection launch the legacy write in a goroutine using a context derived from the request ctx. When the HTTP handler returns, that ctx is cancelled, so context.WithTimeoutCause produces an already-cancelled context and the legacy write fails or is aborted. Mode 3 relies on these writes to keep legacy in sync, so they will often silently not happen. The goroutines should use a detached context (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx)) before applying the timeout.

findings.title: Legacy Create races on the same obj and options that Storage.Create already used
findings.body: The goroutine passes the same obj pointer and options to Legacy.Create while Storage.Create may still be reading or mutating them (e.g. setting ResourceVersion, name generation, or DryRun handling). This is an unsynchronized data race on shared objects. Similarly Update passes the same objInfo to both storage and legacy concurrently, and UpdatedObject may be invoked twice on a one-shot objInfo.

findings.title: Update error path records a legacy metric for a storage failure
findings.body: When Storage.Update fails, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration. This corrupts the legacy error/latency metrics and hides storage failures. The same mistake is in Create's error path (line 45).

findings.title: Create error path records a storage failure as a legacy metric
findings.body: On Storage.Create failure, recordLegacyDuration is called. Storage failures should be recorded with recordStorageDuration, otherwise dashboards show legacy errors for unified-storage failures.

findings.title: Delete records the object name as the resource kind label
findings.body: recordStorageDuration is called with `name` in the kind position (`mode3Str, name, method`), while every other call uses options.Kind. This produces high-cardinality, wrong metric labels per object.

findings.title: DeleteCollection records legacy duration using the storage metric
findings.body: The goroutine calls d.recordStorageDuration for the legacy DeleteCollection result instead of recordLegacyDuration, so legacy failures are counted against storage.

findings.title: Legacy update errors are only counted, never logged
findings.body: Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection drop the legacy error after recording the metric. Failures to write to legacy are therefore invisible to operators except as a counter, and the object is left inconsistent with no log line with the object name to reconcile it.

findings.title: Delete attaches the bare logger to ctx instead of the named one
findings.body: ctx is set with klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log), discarding the `log` built with name/kind/method values that is used for the error logs. Downstream logs lose the context fields.

findings.title: Update goroutine: cancel is not deferred on every path and ctx is created before the goroutine's timer starts
findings.body: The timeout context is created outside the start timer and cancel is deferred after startLegacy; this is inconsistent with the other goroutines and makes the timeout include unrelated work. Minor, but it is an unexpected pattern.

findings.title: Tests never verify the asynchronous legacy writes happen
findings.body: The mode 3 tests set up legacy mock expectations but never wait for or assert the goroutine calls (no AssertExpectations/AssertCalled, no sync). The legacy path could be entirely broken and the tests would still pass. The removed legacy-failure cases (e.g. Create error from legacy) are no longer covered either, since legacy errors no longer affect the result.

findings.title: Misleading test name for List error case
findings.body: The case 'error when listing an object in the unified store is not implemented' now asserts a real storage error path, not a not-implemented stub; the name is stale.

findings.title: Unrelated dependency checksums added to go.work.sum
findings.body: The diff adds checksums for grafana-azure-sdk-go, prometheus-alertmanager, and several OpenTelemetry modules that have nothing to do with dual-writer mode 3. These look like incidental go tooling churn and should be explained or dropped from this PR.
